question: Who among the following was not among the convicts sentenced to death by the British Government of India in the Lahore conspiracy case?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Udham Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Udham Singh was not among the convicts sentenced to death in the Lahore conspiracy case.

• The Lahore conspiracy case involved prominent revolutionaries like Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev.

• Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev Thapar, and Shivaram Rajguru were the main convicts who were sentenced to death in this case.

• Udham Singh is famously known for avenging the Jallianwala Bagh massacre by assassinating Michael O'Dwyer in 1940.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Lahore Conspiracy Case**

• The Lahore Conspiracy Case of 1929 was a significant event in the Indian independence movement against British colonial rule.

• It involved the bombing of the Central Legislative Assembly in Delhi on April 8, 1929, by Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt.

• The objective was to protest against repressive laws and to awaken the masses to the cause of Indian freedom.

• Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev were later tried and sentenced to death for their involvement in the conspiracy and for the murder of J.P. Saunders, a British police officer.

• **Bhagat Singh**

• Bhagat Singh was a charismatic freedom fighter who played a pivotal role in the Indian independence movement.

• He is best known for his daring acts against the British Raj, including the bombing of the Central Legislative Assembly and the assassination of J.P. Saunders.

• His execution on March 23, 1931, turned him into a martyr and a symbol of the fight against British colonial rule.
